findings: Per-kind K cannot be applied directly in S3: every S3 sim clip has at most ONE stated size fact and ONE stated speed fact, and each sits on the very row that probe 5 already answers with that fact (T/SIB). Once a row's own fact is excluded, no unpooled S3 row has a same-kind fact in its clip, so a direct per-kind K changes 0 rows. (The 0026 person-speed fact that probe 5 rejected would only apply half of itself to its own row, so it is excluded.)

Cross-kind K is what hurt S3: LOFO on the 14 S3 fact rows gives raw .707, all-kind K .664 (sizes .800->.757, speeds .660->.600), per-kind K .707 (no same-kind fact remains). In D3 the opposite holds: all-kind K .855 beats per-kind K .823 (sizes .787->.843 vs .830; speeds .788->.888 vs .788), and inside pooling P_Kall .951 beats P_Kkind .930. So D3 should keep probe 5's all-kind K.

Pooling per kind (same object and dimension; speeds only with proven motion identity, at least 3 bases) does help S3. On S3 fact rows held out (LOFO), sizes go .800->.914 (7 rows; speeds have no pools of 3 or more). On proxies from the same family (the validation answer of an equivalent row on another test clip of that family, e.g. 0034_seg's boat height 9.42, width 3.27 and wingspan 1.57, 0060's pedestrian 1.87 and yellow-car height 1.65, 0300's car speeds 4.8/9.8), S3 sizes go .800->.909 (32 rows) and S3 speeds .833->.950 (6 rows). On S3's own known rows (validation answers on the test clips), sizes drop .758->.742 (12 rows): 0034_seg is a clip Claude already got right, and pooling there costs width -0.1 and nothing on wingspan or height.

S3 members of a pool should be corrected per kind (K_size from the clip's stated size facts for sizes, K_speed for speeds); D3 members keep probe 5's all-kind K. Against S3 members left raw (as in probe 5's D3 pools) this gives sizes .894->.909 on proxies and .733->.742 on known rows, and is equal on LOFO. Mainly it lifts the wingspan pool from 1.414 to 1.591 (0034_seg label 1.57), because 0035's eagle-length fact corrects its 1.25 wingspan.

Sharing D3 with S3: copying D3's probe-5 K+P value onto the S3 question about the same object and quantity is supported, but slightly worse than recomputing the pool with per-kind S3 members. Measured on the 28 proxied changed rows: +2.6 points for the D3 copy vs +3.4. This also suggests D3's own wingspan pool (1.445, 9 D3 rows) and boat-width pool (2.667, against a 0034_seg label of 3.27) would improve slightly if D3's pools took S3 members per kind (D3 family-proxy sizes .855->.861; about +0.0007 D3, D3's call).

Guard: one size group is clearly two populations. Rock width is 22-24 m seen top-down (0043/0044, where both horizontal sizes are visible: about 2.2 boat lengths) against 8-10 m from side views, where width is the hidden depth. Skipping a group when at least max(2, n/3) members lie more than 1.6x on one side of the median blocks only this group, and costs nothing on any evaluated row.

Twin averaging was checked and rejected. A segmented twin's own read is worse than its original's (S3 known .945 vs .700; geometric mean .864), so probe 5's twin copy is right, and pooled originals propagate to twins by that copy.

D3 fact sharing (DS) adds 1 row: 0040's malformed 'average of the person at 1.0s' 1.0 -> 1.3. Its person has the same timed depth entries as 0039's, whose D3 speed is the 1.3 m/s sibling fact, and 0034_seg's validation answer for the person speed is 1.3.

Size of the lever: S3 sim/seg rows in multi-clip families with at least 3 equivalent bases number about 45 of 244. The rest of S3 sim, and all 334 lab rows, have no family facts to use, so this lever is worth about +0.006 S3 (+0.0015 MRA), not the +0.06 needed.
